title: LexisNexis and OpenAI Announce Plan to Deliver Custom AI Technology for Legal Professionals
author: LexisNexis Legal & Professional

dom.t: Legal platforms: Content and governance differentiate workflows

st.t: Legal platforms: Content and governance differentiate workflows
st.an: The source supports the cluster’s core proposition by presenting legal-AI differentiation as a combination of task-specific multi-model selection, fine-tuning, trusted legal-content retrieval, integrated workflows and governance safeguards. Its productivity, accuracy and reliability benefits remain vendor claims rather than comparative evidence, and its broad description of autonomous task execution does not itself establish lawyer-guided verification at the point of reliance.
qs: As part of the company's multi-model approach that selects the best AI model for each legal task, including custom LLMs, LexisNexis has leveraged OpenAI models in its products since 2022.

A proprietary Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) platform grounds large language model (LLM) answers in a comprehensive repository of trusted legal content and metadata, delivering high-quality answers and validated citations.

kp.k: Planned OpenAI integration targets personalized legal workflows
kp.d: The 2025 announcement sets out plans to deploy OpenAI APIs and fine-tuned models across LexisNexis products, including Lexis+ AI and the Protégé personalized assistant. LexisNexis also plans to jointly develop models for sophisticated legal workflows requiring enhanced reasoning. These are announced deployment and development plans rather than reported findings about their effects.
qs: announced their plan to deploy OpenAI's APIs and fine-tuned models across the LexisNexis ecosystem of products like the Lexis+ AI® legal workflow solution and LexisNexis Protégé™ personalized AI assistant

LexisNexis will directly leverage OpenAI's latest models and jointly develop fine-tuned models for sophisticated legal workflows that depend on generative AI technology for enhanced "chain of thought" reasoning.

kp.k: Collaboration extends an existing multi-model strategy
kp.d: LexisNexis states that it has used OpenAI models since 2022 within a strategy of selecting models by legal task, including custom LLMs. CTO Jeff Reihl presents direct collaboration as a way to accelerate model customization and product integration. The company describes AWS, Anthropic, Microsoft, Mistral and OpenAI as supporting partners, rather than presenting this agreement as an exclusive model relationship.
qs: As part of the company's multi-model approach that selects the best AI model for each legal task, including custom LLMs, LexisNexis has leveraged OpenAI models in its products since 2022.
Our direct collaboration with OpenAI allows us to accelerate this innovation.

Its multi-model approach selects the best AI model for each use case, and model fine-tuning ensures high performance of domain-specific, personalized LLMs, supported by partners AWS, Anthropic, Microsoft, Mistral, and OpenAI.

kp.k: Executives anticipate productivity gains and simpler legal workflows
kp.d: LexisNexis's Jeff Reihl characterizes personalized AI as enabling faster, enhanced outcomes for legal and business professionals. OpenAI COO Brad Lightcap anticipates faster legal insight gathering, greater productivity and simplified complex workflows for thousands of LexisNexis customers. These are executive expectations; the announcement supplies no measured productivity or work-quality results.
qs: "At LexisNexis, we are dedicated to delivering high-quality, highly personalized AI innovation for legal and business professionals to achieve faster, enhanced outcomes," stated Jeff Reihl, EVP and Chief Technology Officer at LexisNexis Legal & Professional.

"We're thrilled to use our most advanced AI models to power new use cases that accelerate productivity, help gather legal insights faster, and simplify complex workflows for thousands of customers on LexisNexis' platform," said Brad Lightcap, Chief Operating Officer at OpenAI.

kp.k: Platform combines retrieval, content generation and independent task execution
kp.d: LexisNexis describes its platform as integrating extractive AI for finding results and insights, generative AI for creating content from prompts, and agentic AI for independently performing tasks on users' behalf. This describes a claimed expansion in supported task types, without identifying particular autonomous legal workflows or reporting their performance.
qs: The LexisNexis global technology platform seamlessly integrates each wave of AI innovation, including extractive AI, which finds relevant results within data and provides deep insights; generative AI, which excels at creating new content from data based on user-entered prompts or instruction; and agentic AI, which can intelligently and independently perform tasks on a user's behalf.

kp.k: Legal-content grounding and oversight underpin claimed AI reliability
kp.d: LexisNexis attributes answer quality and validated citations to proprietary retrieval augmented generation grounded in legal content and metadata. It describes human oversight, encryption and privacy protections, and states that over 2,000 technologists, data scientists and experts develop, test and validate solutions under RELX Responsible AI Principles. These are descriptions of safeguards and development resources, not quantified accuracy findings.
qs: The company responsibly develops safe AI solutions with human oversight, backed by advanced encryption and privacy technology.

A proprietary Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) platform grounds large language model (LLM) answers in a comprehensive repository of trusted legal content and metadata, delivering high-quality answers and validated citations.
The company employs over 2,000 technologists, data scientists, and experts to develop, test, and validate solutions in line with RELX Responsible AI Principles.

kp.k: Agreement includes internal adoption of ChatGPT Enterprise
kp.d: Alongside customer-facing legal AI development, the agreement provides for LexisNexis global teams to use ChatGPT Enterprise. The announcement anticipates internal productivity gains and faster innovation addressing customer needs, rather than reporting realized benefits.
qs: Additionally, as part of the agreement, LexisNexis global teams will expedite their own productivity benefits, including accelerating innovation to address customers' core needs, via ChatGPT Enterprise.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: LexisNexis and OpenAI plan to deploy and jointly fine-tune models for personalized legal workflows, claiming gains in productivity, work quality, and economic value.
pts.d: The corporate announcement describes planned integration of OpenAI APIs and fine-tuned models into products including Lexis+ AI and Protégé. LexisNexis CTO Jeff Reihl says direct collaboration will accelerate customized legal-AI innovation and faster, enhanced outcomes. OpenAI COO Brad Lightcap predicts faster legal insights, greater productivity, and simpler complex workflows. These are attributed product-benefit claims and plans, rather than reported measurements of legal-service outcomes.

pts.k: LexisNexis says combining extractive, generative, and agentic AI enables information retrieval, content creation, and independent task execution, delivering value faster.
pts.d: The announcement describes extractive AI as finding relevant information and insights, generative AI as creating content from instructions, and agentic AI as independently performing tasks for users. It claims its platform integrates these capabilities to improve customer outcomes and speed delivery of value. It does not identify particular legal tasks completed autonomously or predict replacement of lawyers; its development description also specifies human oversight.

pts.k: LexisNexis claims legal-content grounding, model selection, and fine-tuning produce higher-quality, accurate, personalized legal-AI answers and validated citations.
pts.d: The company presents proprietary retrieval-augmented generation grounded in trusted legal content and metadata as the mechanism for high-quality answers and validated citations. It further claims task-specific model selection and fine-tuning ensure domain-specific performance, while its infrastructure supports continuing improvements in quality, accuracy, and speed. No quantified accuracy or citation-validation results accompany these claims.

pts.k: LexisNexis predicts its own employees will gain productivity and accelerate customer-focused innovation through ChatGPT Enterprise.
pts.d: This is a separate internal operational claim about the legal-technology vendor, rather than a claim about law-firm staffing or clients' legal costs.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The source relies on corporate descriptions of technology, prior deployment experience, development resources, and executive assertions; it supplies no outcome benchmarks or customer case studies.
pts.d: The announcement cites use of OpenAI models since 2022, describes RAG, model selection and fine-tuning, and reports more than 2,000 staff developing, testing, and validating solutions. Reihl and Lightcap provide executive authority for the expected benefits. These constitute the stated experience and technical rationale, not measured evidence of time savings, improved legal work, financial returns, or autonomous-task reliability. The source provides no study design, comparative data, numerical performance results, or concrete customer cases.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The 2025 announcement promises swift deployment and ongoing improvements, but gives no launch deadline or quantified period for realizing benefits.
pts.d: The new collaboration and joint fine-tuning are prospective, whereas OpenAI-model use since 2022 and the platform's described capabilities are presented as existing. Expected improvements depend on integration of newer models, legal-task-specific selection, customization, and grounding in legal content. Security, compliance, privacy, and human oversight are presented as operating safeguards, not independently demonstrated guarantees. No rollout sequence or detailed limits on agentic autonomy are specified.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The claimed beneficiaries are legal and business professionals using LexisNexis products and LexisNexis's own global teams.
pts.d: Customer-facing effects are described as personalized assistance, faster insights, simpler workflows, better work quality, and economic value for thousands of platform customers. Internal effects concern employee productivity and faster innovation. LexisNexis is acting as a legal-technology and information vendor, not an ALSP delivering legal work. The announcement does not distinguish effects on law firms versus in-house departments, junior versus senior lawyers, or particular client segments, and makes no concrete prediction about employment, billing models, market displacement, or access to justice. Its stated reach of more than 150 countries describes the company, not confirmed deployment of the new collaboration throughout those markets.
